analysis.title: The KOSPI crash: how much more pain
key_insights: KOSPI closed decisively below the 5,000 level in another overnight sell-off. The death cross flagged in early November remains in place, and the report sees no meaningful support until the 4,200 area.
KOSPI has been deeply oversold for weeks and the selling continues. The report warns that oversold can stay oversold much longer than most expect.

KOSPI is approaching its 100-week moving average and weekly RSI is at its most oversold level in recent memory. The 200-week moving average is around 3,600. The report does not say KOSPI must reach it, but notes other parabolic manias have unwound all the way back to their long-term averages.

The report compares the KOSPI unwind to silver's recent collapse and says the report's earlier calls that both were making major tops were laughed at. KOSPI is still up on the year, so if silver is a guide there could be considerably more downside.

KOSPI VIX is up from its early October lows but the reaction is muted relative to the size of the sell-off. The report's explanation is that investors are dumping longs and stopping out rather than buying puts.

GS prime brokerage data shows hedge funds dumping Asian AI/tech exposure, with long sales outpacing short sales 2.4 to 1. Korea and Taiwan dominate the selling, with funds both selling longs and adding shorts. Net allocation to Korea is back to levels last seen in early January.
SK Hynix has just flashed a death cross. The report calls it the poster child of the Asian AI mania and says it is not a technical signal to trade against even though valuation looks very cheap.
Goldman's Privorotsky says SK Hynix looks extraordinarily cheap on a blended 24-month P/E, but earnings sustainability is the issue. If estimates come down, the stock can get a lot cheaper.
Privorotsky says the valuation cushion is becoming meaningful, which makes it hard to press the short in SK Hynix. For a bearish view on AI and growth, there may be better places to express it.

market_movers.rationale: SK Hynix flashed a death cross, a technical warning, while the stock looks very cheap on a blended 24-month P/E. Goldman's Privorotsky sees earnings sustainability as the risk and finds the short hard to press.

sector_views.rationale: GS prime brokerage data shows hedge funds selling Asian AI/tech longs at 2.4 times the pace of short sales, led by Korea and Taiwan, with fresh shorts added.

earnings_insights: SK Hynix trades at an extraordinarily cheap blended 24-month P/E per Goldman's Privorotsky. The risk is earnings sustainability, and falling estimates would make the stock cheaper still.
risk_factors: KOSPI has no meaningful support until about 4,200, and the 200-week moving average is near 3,600.
Trapped investors turn short-term trades into long-term holdings, which slows the unwind of a bubble.
SK Hynix earnings estimates could be cut, which would lower the stock further despite its cheap valuation.

KOSPI weekly RSI is at its most oversold level in recent memory, and the index is approaching its 100-week moving average.
